name: translate
title: Translate
description: Translate what you type, the selected text or the clipboard as you type, with the source detected: the translation as the first row (copy, paste, speak), the alternatives, a romanisation when the script is not Latin, dictionary entries for a word, and a Swap row. Google's web endpoint without a key, or DeepL with one; a history of what you copied.
author: pal

settings.label: From
settings.description: The source language as a code or a name (`en`, `turkish`); `auto` detects it. A prefix in the query (`en>tr`) overrides it once.

settings.label: To
settings.description: The target language as a code or a name; empty is the system language. Text already in it is translated the other way. A prefix (`tr:`, `>de`) overrides it once.

settings.label: Backend
settings.description: Google is the web app's unofficial endpoint, no key, with alternatives and romanisation; DeepL needs a key (the free tier does) and answers the translation alone.

settings.label: DeepL API key
settings.description: From deepl.com/your-account/keys; a free key ends in `:fx`. Only read when the backend is DeepL.

settings.label: Speak on copy
settings.text: Also read the translation aloud when Enter copies it (cmd+shift+s speaks either way)

store.tagline: Translate typed, selected or copied text as you type
features: Translated as you type, 350 ms after the last key; the source language detected, the target from the `to` setting or the system language
A prefix names the target once: `tr: hello`, `>de hello`, `en>tr merhaba`, `german: hello`; at the root those answer inline under a Translate section
Nothing typed: the selected text in the app in front, else the newest clipboard text

Rows: the translation (Enter copies, cmd+Enter pastes, cmd+shift+s speaks it aloud), the detected language, the alternatives, a romanisation of either side when the script is not Latin, dictionary entries for a word, and Swap, which translates the result back
Google's web endpoint without a key (unofficial: it may refuse a network it takes for a bot, or change), or DeepL with a free key
Translation History: what was copied, pasted or spoken, newest first, with Translate again

screenshots.caption: hello world typed with the system language Turkish: the translation first, the detected language, the alternatives, Swap
tr>en merhaba dünya. Nasılsın?: both ends named in the prefix; the detail pane shows both texts and the pair
>ja hello: the Japanese with its romanisation and the dictionary entry
What a translation can do: copy, paste, speak, the source, Google Translate
Translation History: what was copied or spoken, newest first

actions.title: Copy
actions.description: The translation onto the clipboard; with `speak` on, read aloud too.

actions.title: Paste
actions.description: Hides, then pastes the translation into the app in front.

actions.title: Speak
actions.description: Reads the row aloud in its language: `say` with a voice of that language on macOS, `spd-say` or `espeak` on Linux.

actions.title: Open in Google Translate
actions.description: The pair and the text in the web app.

actions.title: Swap and translate
actions.description: On the Swap row: the result translated back the other way.

actions.title: Translate again
actions.description: In the history: the entry's text translated afresh.

translate.description: Type text and it is translated to the `to` language (or the system's) with the source detected; `tr: text`, `>de text` or `en>tr text` name the ends once; nothing typed translates the selection, else the clipboard. At the root a prefixed query answers inline.

keys.title: Copy the translation (on Swap: translate it back)
Paste the translation into the app in front

history.description: Translations you copied, pasted or spoke, newest first; Enter copies the translation again.
